title: A Search for Submillimeter H<SUB>2</SUB>O Masers in Active Galaxies: The Detection of 321 GHZ H<SUB>2</SUB>O Maser Emission in NGC 4945
question: Do nearby AGN with strong 22 GHz nuclear H2O masers also host 321/325 GHz H2O masers, and what are their velocities and positions?

what.value: 22 GHz maser position and Keplerian disk model (150 km/s at 0.3 pc, BH mass 1.4e6 Msun)

evidence.quote: which yielded a black hole mass of 1.4 $\times$ 10$^6$ M$_{\ensuremath{\odot}}\;$.

recipe.method: Inspect continuum-subtracted cubes within ~18 arcsec field for features above 5 sigma
Gaussian fits of phase-referenced peak positions; compare maser with continuum peak with error beam/(2 SNR)
Keplerian v ∝ r^-0.5 scaling from 22 GHz disk model

answer_key.quantity: Strongest 321 GHz maser peak flux, NGC 4945 (V_LSR=714.4)

evidence.quote: peak flux densities of $\sim$ 45 mJy beam$^{-1}$ at V$_{\rm LSR}$= 714.4 km s$^{-1}\;$

answer_key.quantity: Total integrated intensity of maser features

evidence.quote: is $\sim$ 2.6 Jy km s$^{-1}$, which corresponds to $\sim$ 7.4 L$_{\ensuremath{\odot}}$.
The continuum peak flux density at this resolution is 136.5 mJy beam$^{-1}$
the maser is located at a distance of $\sim$0.020 pc from the central engine
